Alright, I’ve been digging through the UI layout code in src/tui.tsx to understand how the live items, thoughts, and stream are rendered. The current implementation uses a nested structure with a fixed height (`height={termRows}`) and a `column-reverse` box to keep the newest live items at the bottom. This works but creates an unwanted blank gap above the input when the static scrollback pushes content up – the fixed height forces the dynamic region to occupy the full terminal height, so newly flushed static lines can push the live region off‑screen, leading to the “text jumps to the top / have to scroll up” problem.

I need to rework this layout so that the dynamic region (live items, thoughts, stream) is content‑sized rather than forced to fill the entire terminal. That way the static scrollback can grow without leaving a large empty space. The simplest way is to drop the outer `<Box flexDirection="column" height={termRows} overflow="hidden">` wrapper and the inner `<Box flexDirection="column" flexGrow={1} flexShrink={1} overflow="hidden">` that contains the column‑reverse logic. Instead, I’ll introduce a single `<Box flexDirection="column">` that renders the live items in normal order (no reverse), then the thoughts panel, then the stream. This preserves the visual order (live at top, thoughts, then stream) while allowing the container to size itself to its children. I’ll also add a comment explaining why this region must stay dynamic and not fixed‑height, referencing the push/trimLive/ticker budgets that already keep it short.

To make the change, I’ll locate the exact JSX block that starts with `<Box flexDirection="column" height={termRows} overflow="hidden">` and ends with the closing `</Box>` that encloses the nested column‑reverse layout. I’ll replace that whole block with the new structure I just described. I’ll set `replace_all` to false because I only want to replace this specific occurrence, not any other similar snippets that might exist elsewhere.

Now I’ll construct the edit tool call with:
- `file_path` pointing to src/tui.tsx,
- `old_string` containing the exact original JSX block (including the column‑reverse logic, thoughts, and stream sections),
- `new_string` containing the revised JSX with the comment, a simple `<Box flexDirection="column">`, live items rendered directly, then the thoughts block, then the stream block.

This should fix the layout issue by removing the fixed height and reverse ordering, making the UI behave more naturally.

arguments.old_string:
<Box flexDirection="column" height={termRows} overflow="hidden">
      <Box flexDirection="column" flexGrow={1} flexShrink={1} overflow="hidden">
      <Box flexDirection="column-reverse">
        {/* Stream + thinking render first so column-reverse puts them at the bottom */}
        {stream ? (
          <Box flexDirection="row">
            <Box width={2} flexShrink={0}>
              <Text color={theme.orange}>✦</Text>
            </Box>
            <Box flexDirection="column" flexGrow={1}>
              <Markdown text={stream} />
            </Box>
          </Box>
        ) : null}

        {running && thoughtsOn && thoughtLines.length > 0 && (
          <Box flexDirection="column" borderStyle="round" borderColor={theme.faint} paddingX={1}>
            <Text color={theme.dim}>
              {thoughtExpanded ? "▾" : "▸"} thinking{" "}
              <Text color={theme.faint}>(click or ctrl+t to {thoughtExpanded ? "collapse" : "expand"})</Text>
            </Text>
            {thoughtExpanded ? (
              thoughtLines.slice(-12).map((l, i) => (
                <Text key={i} color={theme.faint} italic>
                  {"  "}
                  {l.slice(0, 200)}
                </Text>
              ))
            ) : (
              <Text color={theme.faint} italic>
                {"  "}
                {lastThought.slice(-160) || "…"}
              </Text>
            )}
          </Box>
        )}

        {/* Live items reversed so newest renders at bottom with column-reverse */}
        {liveItems.slice().reverse().map((item) => (
          <ItemView key={item.id} item={item} />
        ))}
      </Box>
      </Box>
